sanjay: quick summary from the overnight long-ctx+quant runs — posting raw notes here so we can triage. INT8 reduces KV backing memory ~3.8x vs bf16, throughput +22% on the fused int8 kernel, but we're seeing a ~1.7% nLL/regression on long-context prompts when KV pages get paged and then reused. link: https://perf.internal/runs/1943335 :eyes:

lia: can you paste the kernel selection trace and the exact bench command? want to see whether the runtime switched kernels mid-request (that can alter rounding). also which batching policy?

sanjay: bench command + flags:
```bash
./bench_run --model rwd-7b --seq-len 32768 --quant int8 --kv-pages=8192 --batch-policy=latency-prefer --kernel-pick=auto --kv-warmup=on 
```
kernel log snippet:
```
kernel-picker: selected fused-int8-gemm (v3) for seq<=512
kernel-picker: fallback to bf16-gemm for matmul(1024) due to precision-guard
kv: page_hit=0.62 page_reuse=0.41 compaction_skipped=7
```

matt: saw something related in canary earlier — page boundary fragmentation seems to make the reuse heuristic over-assign partial pages to new slots. small holes -> later merges result in pages reused with stale kv meta; combined with int8 quantization noise that tips generation probabilities. can we add a quick histogram of free-span sizes?

anya: pasted sample eviction log from the failing run:
```
[2025-11-12T03:12:06Z] evict_page id=0x7f2 size=4096 used=3832 free=264 age_windows=2 last_access=1024
[2025-11-12T03:12:06Z] alloc_page id=0x7f9 size=4096 used=16 free=4080
[2025-11-12T03:12:06Z] kv_read miss addr=0x7f2 offset=3584 -> trigger page_pull
```
observations: frequent small allocations after heavy long prefixes; free-span histogram is spiky at powers-of-two (64/256/4096) which points to internal slab fragmentation.

ci-bot: CI test 'kv-memory-stability (int8-longctx)' failed on canary: peak_rss increased 18% after 2h ramp. logs: https://ci.internal/builds/9001

lia: do we have a concise repro that isolates precision vs reuse? e.g., run same workload with exact same kernel selection but force kv eviction to be deterministic (no compaction) then run with bf16 vs int8. that will tell us whether the regression is quant->kernel or quant->kv-interaction.

sanjay: yep did that. short results:
- forced-deterministic-evict + bf16: baseline nLL
- forced-deterministic-evict + int8: ~0.4% nLL regression
- default-evict (current heuristics) + bf16: ~0.2% regression (likely due to page-reuse mismatch)
- default-evict + int8: ~1.7% regression
so both effects add. int8 amplifies small probability shifts caused by suboptimal reuse/fragmentation.

matt: hypothesis: when a page gets reused across different relative-position contexts, the KV index's occupancy + quant noise shift logits enough to change top-k on borderline tokens. int8 kernels do slightly different accumulation order / rounding -> combine to nudge the final token.

anya: suggested short-term mitigations:
1) increase kv-warmup window from 1->4 for int8 canaries (less aggressive reuse until a slot is 'hot')
2) enable opportunistic compaction in background during low-traffic windows (coalesce spans > threshold)
3) fallback to bf16 for the first 2 decoder layers if observed recall delta > 1% during A/B runs

sanjay: I'm landing a canary with (1) + modified reallocate heuristics: prefer allocating from largest-fit free spans first to reduce tiny-hole proliferation. config snippet:
```json
{"kv.warmup_windows":4, "kv.compactor.background":true, "kv.alloc_strategy":"largest_fit"}
```
will open A/B with 20% of traffic. metrics to watch: page_reuse, page_hit, nLL, peak_rss, p99-latency.

lia: can you also dump kernel fp error stats? e.g., per-op max_abs_diff between bf16 and int8 fused gemm across the batch. if we can localize to a small set of layers / token positions we can try per-layer mixed precision.

matt: quick patch idea for compactor — run async compaction that respects a 'min_hotness' threshold so we don't compact active tail pages. pseudocode:
```
for span in free_spans:
  if span.size < MIN_COMPACT_SIZE: continue
  if span.last_used + cooldown < now: coalesce(span)
```
this avoids background thrash.

deploy-bot: deploy started for canary/int8-kv-heuristic v2025.11.12-rc3 -> capacity: 20% (hosts: canary-3, canary-4)

anya: quick note on evals — we ran 2k long-context prompts (docs+code mix). -> int8 + default heuristics had 14 prompts with top-1 change that produced factual drift vs bf16; after warmup_windows=4 that dropped to 3. precision-savvy approach seems promising.

sanjay: good. collecting traces for the 3 residual failures to see whether it's still a page-reuse pattern or a pure kernel rounding corner. i'll attach diff traces here when available.

lia: if the compactor helps, we should make the allocator expose diagnostic telemetry (free-span distribution, compaction-stepped, coalesces/sec) so SREs can watch long-running hosts. add to roadmap for 'kv-observability' panel.

matt: also add a small unit-test that simulates interleaved long prefixes to assert no page-runaway after X steps. we had an old one but it didn't exercise large seq lengths.

ci-bot: test triggered: 'kv-alloc-stress (canary-config)' -> queued

anya: thanks team. next steps: sanjay runs AB for 24h, lia gathers kernel-err stats, matt lands compactor minimal, I'll correlate eval diffs to exact token positions. ping me if you want me to triage any specific residual samples. :thumbsup:

sanjay: thanks — will update in this thread with traces + perf dashboards. :eyes:
